breadcrumbSchema.name: Top 10 Stays near Wua Lai Walking Street, Chiang Mai

introH2: 🛍️ Why is the Wua Lai walking street area a good place to stay in Chiang Mai?
introHtml: Wua Lai is the historic silversmiths' street south of the old city moat, in Haiya subdistrict, and every Saturday evening it turns into the Saturday walking street — every bit as lively as the Sunday walking street in the old town, with local food, silver craft, and Wat Sri Suphan (the Silver Temple), whose ordination hall is built entirely from silver, as the centerpiece · the upside of this area is that it's still a real residential neighbourhood for Chiang Mai locals, so room prices are more affordable than in the old town or Nimman, and it's only a 5–10 minute drive from Chiang Mai airport, so you don't have to leave huge buffers on the morning you fly out · this article rounds up 10 Wua Lai stays we've reviewed across every level — from garden boutiques to value-for-money guesthouses and design hostels, every one based on reading real guest reviews, comparing prices across 3 sites, and giving you a full set of direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Chiang Mai has no metro, but the Wua Lai area is compact and easy to get around on foot · from Chiang Mai airport (CNX) it's only about 5–10 min by car to Wua Lai, closer than many areas · the key spots around the neighbourhood: the Saturday walking street — open every Saturday evening with food, craft and silver · Wat Sri Suphan (the Silver Temple) — an ordination hall built entirely of silver, the symbol of the area · Chiang Mai Gate — a short walk away, with the Chiang Mai Gate market and evening food, and direct access into the southern old town · Nantaram Road — on the Haiya side, a quieter local area that connects on foot to Wua Lai · calling a Grab or a red truck (songthaew) into the old town and Nimman is easy too.

entries.name: Wualai Sabaidee
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wua Lai Soi 3 · walk to the walking street and Silver Temple
tags: 🚶 Walk to the Wua Lai walking street
entries.addr: 5 Wualai Road Soi 3, Haiya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If we're going to open the list with the highest-scoring stay in this article, it has to be Wualai Sabaidee — 9.7 on Agoda from 352 reviews, and plenty of real reviews agree it feels more like staying at a friend's house than checking into a hotel · it's a small Lanna-style boutique guesthouse of around 16 rooms, on Soi 3 in the Wua Lai area, with the rooms arranged around a green garden in the middle of the building · the thing reviews mention most often is the cleanliness — many call it cleaner than the price would suggest — and the quiet garden in the centre, which some describe as an oasis in a busy part of town · service is a strong point too: the staff are warm and friendly, happy to suggest places to go and call cars for you, but they also give you enough personal space without hovering · the location is a big bonus — about 350 metres' walk to the Wua Lai walking street on Saturday nights, with Wat Sri Suphan (the Silver Temple) within walking distance, plus free bikes to borrow for riding into the old town; many reviews say they barely needed a car the whole trip · to be honest about the caveats from the reviews — there's no pool or spa on site, there's some neighbourhood traffic noise in the morning as you'd expect from a stay in town, and some Standard rooms are fairly compact and have no balcony · light sleepers should ask for a room facing the garden · in short, if you want a clean room, a quiet garden, warm service and a base for exploring the silversmiths' quarter on a budget of a few thousand baht, this is the best-value option in the area.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a room with a balcony over the garden for more quiet and a nicer setting, and check the breakfast details directly with the property before booking, as they differ from one platform to another.
pros: Highest score in this article, 9.7 from 352 reviews
Quiet green garden, feels like staying in a home
Free bikes to borrow, walk to the Wua Lai walking street and the Silver Temple
Warm, friendly staff who also give you personal space
cons: Small property, no pool or spa on site
Some Standard rooms are fairly compact

entries.name: The Entaneer Poshtel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Haiya·Nantaram · walk to Chiang Mai Gate
tags: 🔒 Curtain, plug and locker at every bed
entries.addr: 93/1 Nantaram Road, Haiya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If you're on the tightest budget but still want good design and a good night's sleep, The Entaneer Poshtel deserves a spot on the list — 9.5 from 711 reviews, with prices starting at just ฿450 a bed · the name Poshtel comes from "posh" plus "hostel", a hostel that pushes comfort up close to a hotel's, and what real reviews mention most is the dorms with no bunk beds — every bed is at floor level, with walls on three sides plus a blackout curtain on the fourth, and a plug, reading light and personal locker; some reviews say it feels like having your own little room, so you sleep well without worrying about anyone else · the building is a renovated old factory in industrial-loft style — bare concrete, black steel, old wood — that many say photographs beautifully, unlike a typical hostel · breakfast is included and the made-to-order eggs are cooked fresh, another thing people praise · it's run by a local family, and the staff and hosts are praised for looking after you like a friend, with activities like market walks and cooking classes so solo travellers can make friends · the honest caveat from the reviews is that the vibe leans calm — this isn't a party hostel — and one solo female traveller wrote about feeling uncomfortable during a group activity, so choosing the women-only dorm is the more comfortable option · it's just a 2–3 minute walk to the Wua Lai walking street, near Chiang Mai Gate, with free parking and close to the airport — a good fit for budget travellers who value a proper night's sleep.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: solo female travellers should choose the Female Dorm, and book ahead on Saturdays and during festivals, as this is a small property that fills up fast.
pros: Dorms with no bunk beds, with walls and a curtain that make each bed feel like a private room
Old-factory loft design that photographs well
Very clean, comfortable beds, made-to-order eggs at breakfast
Prices from just ฿450, walk to the Wua Lai walking street, free parking
cons: A calm hostel, not a heavily social one
No resort-style pool or spa

entries.name: iSilver Hotel
entries.badge: 🏊 With a pool, best value in the area
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wua Lai Soi 3 · walk to the Saturday walking street
tags: 🍳 Fresh breakfast with a changing daily menu
entries.addr: 16/1 Wua Lai Road Soi 3, Hai Ya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: iSilver Hotel is the 3-star boutique hotel in the Wua Lai area that real reviews describe most often with the same phrase: better value than the price, scoring 9.4 from 636 reviews · it opened in 2018 with a "Less is More" concept, focusing on simple, clean, genuinely usable rooms, on Soi 3 of Wua Lai Road, with 31 rooms · what sets it apart from similarly priced guesthouses in the area is the outdoor saltwater pool, which is gentler on the skin, plus free parking, at a price that's still within reach · the real stars that almost every review agrees on are the people and the breakfast — the staff category scores around 9.8, with smiling staff who remember guests' names and give genuine recommendations for khao soi shops and places to go, while the breakfast buffet changes its menu daily, with fresh eggs, and free water, coffee and snacks around the clock · the beds are comfortable enough that many call them some of the best they slept in all trip, and the rooms are spotless · the honest caveats from the reviews are that the hotel sits down a lane, the lane mouth and walkway are fairly dark at night and on some nights there's barking dogs, the room lighting is on the dim side, it's a small hotel with no gym or spa on site, and the walls and doors don't fully block sound, so you sometimes hear the corridor · it's about a 4 minute walk to Wat Sri Suphan, and the Saturday walking street is right at the mouth of the lane, with the airport about 10 minutes away — a good fit for anyone who wants service and a breakfast that punch above the price in the Wua Lai area.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: travelling as a group or family, look at the roomier Triple or Quadruple rooms, and book ahead in high season as rooms fill fast and prices climb.
pros: An outdoor saltwater pool and free parking, better value than the price
Excellent service, staff remember guests and help out well
Fresh breakfast with a changing daily menu · free water, coffee and snacks 24h
Walk to the Silver Temple and the Saturday walking street, close to the airport
cons: Down a lane; the lane mouth and walkway are fairly dark at night
A small hotel of 31 rooms, no gym/spa, and the walls don't fully block sound

entries.type: Boutique Hotel, 3-Star · on the Walking Street
entries.name: iWualai Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wua Lai Road · on the Saturday walking street
tags: 🍳 Varied breakfast with a frequently changing menu
entries.addr: 84 Wualai Road, Hai Ya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If you want to be as close to the Saturday walking street as possible, iWualai Hotel is the most direct option — right on Wua Lai Road at number 84, scoring 9.1 from 450 reviews · it's a small boutique hotel of just 30 rooms that opened in 2016 with the same "Less is More" concept as its sibling iSilver, with a relaxed, quiet atmosphere · what real reviews praise most often and most consistently is the breakfast — a buffet mixed with made-to-order dishes that many say changes its menu almost every day, so you don't get bored over several nights, cooked fresh and of good quality, enough that many cite it as the reason they come back · the staff are praised just as much, remembering guests, suggesting restaurants and places to go, calling cars, and looking after late check-ins in a friendly way · the rooms are clean, the beds soft, and there's an outdoor saltwater pool and free parking that are hard to find in the area · the honest caveats from the reviews are that there are fairly few power outlets in the rooms for anyone carrying several devices, the shower is wall-mounted rather than a handheld one, the pool water is fairly cold in the cool season, and the market is lively on Saturday evenings so there can be some noise out front — which many actually see as part of the charm, since you step out the door and you're right in the action · it's about 200–300 metres from Wat Sri Suphan, an easy walk to the old town, and about 10 minutes from the airport — a good fit for couples and small families who want to step out of the stay straight onto the walking street.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're coming on a Saturday night for the market, this location is excellent value, but if you want a quiet night ask for a room not facing the main road, and bring your own power strip in case the in-room outlets aren't enough.
pros: Location right on the Saturday walking street, walk to the Silver Temple and the old town
Varied breakfast with a frequently changing menu, widely praised
Outdoor saltwater pool and free parking
Warm staff who help with recommendations and calling cars
cons: Fairly few power outlets in the rooms, wall-mounted shower
The market is lively on Saturday evenings, so there can be noise out front

entries.name: Norn-Nanta House
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Haiya·Nantaram · on the Wua Lai walking street
tags: 🏔️ Upper-floor rooms with Doi Suthep views
🚶 On the Wua Lai walking street
entries.addr: 38/2 Nantaram Road, Hai Ya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Norn-Nanta House is a B&B-style guesthouse run by the owner and their family, with a big stack of 697 reviews, a score of 9.1 and prices from just ฿750 · it's on Nantaram Road in the Haiya area, and what real reviews mention almost everywhere is the homely feeling — many say it's more like staying at a relative's house than a hotel · the owner gives a warm welcome, suggesting local restaurants, cycling routes and spots most people overlook, plus there are free bikes to borrow and coffee, tea, snacks and fruit set out to help yourself to all day, which makes it great value · the rooms are clean with brightly painted walls, and many reviews say they're bigger than expected, with the highlight being the upper-floor rooms with a private balcony looking out to Doi Suthep, a spot many guests say they liked best · the location scores high too — Booking rates the location around 9.5 — on the Wua Lai walking street, walk to Chiang Mai Gate and the old town, only 5–10 minutes from the airport · the honest caveats from the reviews are that there's no lift, so you carry your bags up the stairs, the hot water is sometimes inconsistent, the power in some rooms cuts off when no one is in, and there are only free snacks rather than a breakfast buffet — which isn't a problem since the Chiang Mai Gate market is within walking distance · the owner's English isn't very fluent, but Thai speakers will be very comfortable · budget travellers who want a warm homely feel and a good location will like it here.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for an upper-floor King room with a Doi Suthep view if you want the mountain outlook, and pack light since there's no lift · the owner speaks Thai easily, so communicating is simple.
pros: Attentive, friendly owner who can recommend restaurants and places to go
Free bikes, free coffee, tea, snacks and fruit, great value
On the Wua Lai walking street, walk to Chiang Mai Gate and the old town
Upper-floor rooms have a balcony with Doi Suthep views · close to the airport
cons: No lift, you carry your bags up the stairs
No breakfast buffet, only free snacks · hot water is sometimes inconsistent

entries.name: Hotel De Wualai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wua Lai Soi 5 · walk to the Saturday walking street
tags: 🛏️ Rooms more spacious than the price
entries.addr: 3/3 Wua Lai Road Soi 5, Hai Ya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Hotel De Wualai is a small 4-star boutique hotel of just 23 rooms near the Saturday walking street in the Wua Lai area, scoring 8.8 · it's a step up from the guesthouses in the area, set on Soi 5 of Wua Lai Road, about a 2 minute walk to Wat Sri Suphan (the Silver Temple) and to the walking street itself · what real reviews like is the rooms being more spacious than the price, with many having a private balcony and an in-room jacuzzi tub for a premium feel at a boutique price, plus a rooftop saltwater pool with a whirlpool that looks out over the Wua Lai area · the strongest point that reviews praise repeatedly is the service — the staff are friendly, warm and more helpful than expected, enough that one review is titled "Peaceful & Friendly" · breakfast is simple but good, with made-to-order eggs, and the location is only 5–10 minutes from the airport · the honest caveats to give in full are that sound insulation between rooms isn't great, the hot-water pressure and temperature in some bathrooms is inconsistent, the pool water is cold in the cool season, and some older reviews mention bed bugs and unexpected extra charges (e.g. for towels and drinking water) · there aren't many reviews yet (27), so it's worth reading the most recent ones across several platforms, checking the room and asking about in-room charges clearly at check-in, and choosing a room away from the main road if you want quiet · a good fit for couples and culture lovers who value a spacious room and a location in the silver quarter.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: choose Deluxe or above if you want a jacuzzi tub and a spacious room, and read the most recent reviews across several platforms before booking, since the review count is still low.
pros: 4-star, with a rooftop pool and whirlpool
Rooms more spacious than the price, some with an in-room jacuzzi tub

Walk to the Saturday walking street and the Silver Temple · close to the airport

entries.name: Rinn Boutique House
entries.badge: 💰 Good value · balcony with city views
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nantaram·Wua Lai · walk to the Saturday walking street
tags: 🏙️ Balcony with city and mountain views
entries.addr: 52 Nantaram Road, Haiya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Rinn Boutique House is a budget boutique house in the Wua Lai area that real reviews describe with the same phrase: better value than the price, scoring 8.7 from 320 reviews, with prices from ฿900 · it's a multi-storey, clean-lined white-toned house on Nantaram Road that has been open since around 2017 and is still kept in good shape · what reviews praise most often is the cleanliness and rooms that are bigger than expected, kept tidy, with the owner looking after the details closely, from the floor tiles to the bed linen; many rooms have a private balcony looking out to the city and distant mountains, and there are free bikes to borrow for riding into town · the staff are friendly and help out with both luggage and laundry, the Wi-Fi signal is good throughout, and it's close enough to the airport that you don't need a big time buffer on the morning you fly out · it's the kind of stay you don't come to in order to be at the hotel, but to use Chiang Mai as a base and come back to sleep in a spacious, clean room at a light price — a good fit for backpackers, couples on a budget, and anyone set on walking the Saturday walking street · the honest caveats from the reviews are that there's no lift, so upper-floor rooms mean stairs, there's no pool or spa, the beds are fairly firm for anyone who likes a soft mattress, the air-con temperature in some rooms isn't steady, and the location is below the city moat so you walk or ride a bit more to reach the centre of the old town · anyone with heavy bags should ask for a ground-floor room when booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: choose the Superior or Deluxe Balcony if you want a spacious room and a balcony with city views, and borrow a free bike to ride to the Saturday walking street and the Chiang Mai Gate market.
pros: Rooms bigger than expected, spotless, great value
Free bikes to borrow · balcony with city and mountain views
Friendly, helpful staff · good Wi-Fi signal
Walk to the Saturday walking street · close to the airport
cons: No lift, upper-floor rooms mean stairs · beds are fairly firm
Below the city moat, you walk or ride a bit more to reach the centre of the old town

entries.name: Sri Ngachang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wua Lai Soi 2 · walk to the Saturday walking street
tags: 🌿 Old house in a quiet garden
🍳 Fresh breakfast, more generous than the price
entries.addr: 1/2 Wua Lai Road Soi 2, Haiya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Sri Ngachang, or by its Thai name Sri Ngachang House, is a very small garden guesthouse of just 6 rooms on Soi 2 of Wua Lai Road, with prices from just ฿700 and an Agoda score as high as 9.3 · it's a two-storey house in a garden, looked after closely by the owner and a few staff, and anyone who likes a stay that feels like visiting a relative's house in Chiang Mai will get exactly that feeling · what real reviews mention often is the quiet garden atmosphere despite being right by the market area — every room has a balcony with a garden view, soft beds and clean linen — and the fresh breakfast that many say is more generous than the price, with some comparing it to a hot lunch, with dishes and fruit · there's bike rental, car rental and help arranging tours, free private parking, and it's only about 5 km from the airport, within walking distance of the Saturday walking street and Chiang Mai Gate · the caveat to tell in full is that the reviews on service split two ways — most voices on Agoda and Booking praise the staff as lovely and attentive, but some reviews on TripAdvisor complain about communication in tense situations, so it's worth reading the most recent reviews, keeping your booking confirmation and photographing the room's condition on arrival · on top of that, it's an old house in a garden, so be prepared for the odd natural insect, there are only 6 rooms so it fills fast during festivals and on Saturdays, and there's no 24-hour staffed counter, so let them know your arrival time in advance · a good fit for flexible travellers who prefer a homely feel over a hotel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: let the property know your check-in time in advance, as there's no 24-hour counter, and book early on Saturdays and during festivals since there are only 6 rooms.
pros: Quiet garden atmosphere despite being right by the market area
Fresh breakfast, more generous than the price · attentive staff
Walk to the Saturday walking street and Chiang Mai Gate · close to the airport
Free private parking · bike rental, car rental and tour arrangements
cons: An old house in a garden, be prepared for the odd natural insect
Only 6 rooms, fills fast · no 24-hour staffed counter

entries.name: Haikin Ryokan
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wua Lai Road · near Wat Sri Suphan
entries.addr: 142-144 Wua Lai Road, Hai Ya, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Haikin Ryokan is a small Japanese-style boutique ryokan of around 10–14 rooms in the Wua Lai area with its own onsen and sauna, scoring 8.6 from 327 reviews · it has been open since around 2015, born from the owner's wish to bring the feel of a real Japanese ryokan into Chiang Mai's silversmiths' quarter · what sets it apart from other stays in the area is the distinctive, genuinely Japanese atmosphere — minimalist rooms in wood and tatami, with yukata to wear, an in-room wooden bathtub in some rooms, plus a separate men's and women's onsen/communal bath with a sauna and steam room, as if Japan had been lifted into the middle of Chiang Mai without the long flight · the breakfast is a fresh Japanese set, served dish by dish on a pretty tray, a highlight that gets consistent praise; the staff and owner look after you personally and remember guests' faces, there's free parking, it's about a 6 minute walk to Wat Sri Suphan, and it's near the Wua Lai walking street and only 10 minutes by car from the airport · the honest caveats from the reviews are that the price is fairly high relative to the rather small rooms, better for a short stay than a long one, the Wi-Fi in some spots isn't steady enough for work, the building has no lift, the water pressure or hot water sometimes isn't hot enough, and vegetarian/vegan food options are limited · the onsen runs in set time slots, so ask the counter about the times at check-in · a good fit for couples and lovers of Japanese culture who value the experience over square metres.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: choose a room with a wooden bathtub if you want the full ryokan feel, and treat this as a short stay for the experience rather than a long one, since the rooms are fairly small.
pros: A distinctive, genuinely Japanese ryokan atmosphere, unlike a typical stay
Has an onsen/communal bath, sauna, and a wooden tub in some rooms
Fresh Japanese set breakfast, consistently praised
Walk to Wat Sri Suphan and the Wua Lai walking street · free parking
cons: Price is fairly high relative to the rather small rooms
The building has no lift · Wi-Fi in some spots isn't steady enough for work

entries.storyHtml: We close the list with Noble House Chiangmai — the budget guesthouse with the most reviews in this article, at 891, scoring 8.0 with prices from ฿900 · it's a medium-sized guesthouse of 48 rooms on Nantaram Road, open since 2012 and renovated in 2022 · what real reviews mention most often and cite as the main reason for choosing it is the location — it's less than a hundred metres from the stay to the Wua Lai walking street on Saturday nights, another 3 minute walk to Chiang Mai Gate and the Chiang Mai Gate market with food all day, and about 10 minutes from the airport · almost every room has a private balcony, en-suite bathroom, air-con and a TV at a budget price; many reviews say the rooms and balconies are bigger than expected, and the rooms renovated in 2022 are cleaner and brighter than the older zone, so ask for a renovated room when booking · the staff are friendly, allow early check-in when a room is free, and there's a tour counter that helps book cars to Doi Suthep, elephant trips and minivans to Pai and Chiang Rai · the honest caveats from the reviews are that the Wi-Fi in some rooms is weak or unstable, especially rooms far from the router, so bring a backup SIM if you need to work; some reviews got a bed type that didn't match the booking, so confirm it at check-in; the hot water is sometimes unstable; the area is lively and noisy on Saturday nights; and it's a simple guesthouse with no pool or spa, and breakfast isn't included · a good fit for budget travellers who want to stay in the middle of the market area and explore the southern old town on foot.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: reconfirm the bed type at check-in, since some reviews got a bed that didn't match the booking, and if you want a quiet night ask for a room not facing the main road on Saturday nights.

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about staying in the Wua Lai area

faq.q: ❓ Who is the Wua Lai walking street area right for?
faq.a: Wua Lai is right for anyone who wants an affordable stay in an area that's still a real community of Chiang Mai locals, within walking distance of the Saturday walking street, Wat Sri Suphan (the Silver Temple) and Chiang Mai Gate · it suits budget-to-mid-range travellers, people who like a local feel and local food, and anyone who wants to be near the airport for early or late flights · those who want modern cafes and nightlife may be a better fit for Nimman.

faq.q: ❓ How much do stays in the Wua Lai area cost?
faq.a: They're more affordable than the central old town and Nimman: hostels and guesthouses start around ฿450–900 a night (The Entaneer Poshtel, Sri Ngachang, Norn-Nanta House, Noble House) · boutiques and mid-range hotels are around ฿1,300–1,500 (Wualai Sabaidee, iSilver, iWualai, Haikin Ryokan, Hotel De Wualai) · all prices in this article are approximate starting rates from standard rooms, and during festivals (Loy Krathong/Yi Peng in Nov, Songkran, New Year) prices can be higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ What day is the Wua Lai walking street open?
faq.a: The Wua Lai walking street is open every Saturday evening (from about late afternoon into the evening) on Wua Lai Road south of Chiang Mai Gate, with local food, craft, silver and performances · if you're set on walking the market, book a stay in this area and expect the neighbourhood to be lively and noisy on Saturday nights · the Sunday walking street, by contrast, is in the central old town on Ratchadamnoen Road, a different area.

faq.q: ❓ Is the Wua Lai area far from Chiang Mai airport?
faq.a: Very close · Chiang Mai airport (CNX) is only about 5–10 minutes by car from the Wua Lai area, one of the closest areas to the airport in Chiang Mai · calling a Grab from the airport is easiest, and many stays have free parking and some offer a pick-up service · it's a great fit for anyone with an early or late flight, with no need for a big time buffer.

faq.q: ❓ Which stays in the Wua Lai area have a pool?
faq.a: In this article the stays with a pool are iSilver Hotel and iWualai Hotel (outdoor saltwater pools) and Hotel De Wualai (a rooftop pool with a whirlpool) · the guesthouses and hostels in the area, such as Wualai Sabaidee, Norn-Nanta House, Sri Ngachang and The Entaneer Poshtel, have no pool on site, but make up for it with a warm atmosphere and more affordable prices.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a stay in the Wua Lai area?
faq.a: On normal weekdays, booking 2–4 weeks ahead is enough · but many stays in this area are small guesthouses and boutiques with few rooms (Sri Ngachang, for instance, has just 6), so they fill fast, especially on Saturday nights with the walking street and during the Yi Peng/Loy Krathong festival (November), Songkran and New Year, when you should book 1–2 months or more in advance.
